The dip morphology is consistent: near-vertical descent, brief plateau at minimum, near-vertical recovery, no overshoot or ringing. Between dips, the signal is perfectly stable (zero slope, zero roughness, zero curvature), indicating high stationarity over short horizons. Noise is absent (MAD = 0 in all catalog entries), suggesting either strong smoothing or truly deterministic behavior. The only variation across candidates is dip count and placement, which aligns with window length and expected cycle count; no evidence of trend, amplitude drift, or irregular peaks/troughs outside this motif. Acceptable normal variation includes exactly 1–3 such symmetric negative spikes per 240-point window, spaced ~80 points apart, with depth ≈ −10.5 ± 0.5.
